limitations: PROVISIONAL: PR #91 report v1 is an interim input, not the canonical PT-01 interface.
Evidence is a report fragment, not verified source context; symbol-only evidence can originate in comments or strings.
Lexical matches include declarations, same-name identifiers and inactive code; they do not prove a call or platform dependency.
Raw evidence is withheld; locations, matched rule aliases and a SHA-256 digest identify the supplied evidence.
No conversion, execution, capability grant, compatibility certification or target acceptance is performed.

rules.reason: The Windows header indicates a platform-specific dependency candidate.
gaps: Separate platform adapters; the current public SDK does not provide windows.h.

rules.reason: Win32 file opening uses sharing flags, creation dispositions and Windows handles.
gaps: No general file-open API is exposed by this public SDK.
Review path encoding, sharing, creation and permission semantics; do not substitute host file access.

rules.reason: Win32 byte reads use a handle and may use overlapped completion.
gaps: No public general file-read API is available in this SDK.
Partial reads, EOF, completion and errors require explicit adapter design.

rules.reason: Windows handle writes require explicit data-integrity and completion semantics.
gaps: The SDK does not expose a general file-write API.
Review short writes, atomicity, cancellation and durability separately.

rules.reason: A Windows HANDLE is not a Nagi capability and cannot be transferred by numeric reinterpretation.
gaps: No generic Windows handle-close equivalent is exposed by this SDK.
Define lifetime and attenuated rights through the actual service contract.

rules.reason: Windows registry persistence requires a storage redesign.

alternatives.limits: App-scoped state interface only; no registry hierarchy, storage implementation or authority is supplied.

gaps: A runtime storage backend, namespace mapping and migration strategy remain required.
Do not map machine-wide registry authority to app state.

rules.reason: Thread creation and wait-object semantics require a runtime-specific adapter.
gaps: The current public SDK exposes no equivalent threading or wait-object API.

rules.reason: Process launch and shell execution cannot be inferred from application identity helpers.
gaps: No public process-launch client or shell execution equivalent is provided here.
Explicit authorization and a real runtime contract remain required.

rules.reason: Managed process launch needs a runtime adapter and cannot be replaced by SDK identity helpers.
gaps: The public SDK provides no managed runtime or process-launch client.
Resolve short type names and review launch authorization and shell behavior explicitly.

rules.reason: Microsoft CRT file entry points differ in encoding, sharing, errors and invalid-parameter handling.
gaps: No equivalent public SDK file entry points are confirmed.
A portable C rewrite still needs a target libc/PAL and explicit semantics testing; host libc success is insufficient.

rules.reason: Microsoft CRT case, locale, truncation and constraint-handler behavior require a per-function review.
gaps: No direct public SDK replacement is asserted.
Do not treat similarly named standard C functions as semantically equivalent.

rules.reason: .NET managed file I/O depends on runtime, encoding, exception and disposal semantics.
gaps: No .NET execution compatibility or managed file API is exposed by this SDK.
Short type names may refer to unrelated local types; resolve symbols before redesign.

rules.reason: Native Windows UI needs an explicit Nagi UI redesign, not a window ABI substitution.

alternatives.limits: Constructs logical presentation data; does not open a native window, render, connect IPC or grant rights.

gaps: Window creation, event handling, accessibility and rendering are not implemented by this helper.
Hand UI structure and interaction work to PT-04.

rules.reason: WPF managed windows require Nagi UI redesign; .NET is not necessarily a Windows dependency outside Windows-specific frameworks.

alternatives.limits: Logical presentation identity only; no WPF controls, binding, rendering or managed runtime is supplied.

gaps: Rebuild UI structure and interaction through PT-04; do not claim WPF execution compatibility.
